skill.name: enact-hello-simple
skill.description: Prints a fixed hello-world greeting as a minimal Enact example.
skill.summary: Minimal Enact example that prints a fixed greeting.
skill.author: EnactProtocol

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns in this prompt-only skill. Manual review found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable workflow beyond a fixed greeting command.

content.value_statement: New Enact users need a minimal example that is easy to inspect. This skill shows a prompt-only hello-world command for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Prints a fixed greeting message through an echo command.
Provides a minimal Enact skill manifest with name, version, command, and tags.
Demonstrates a hello-world style skill structure in one SKILL.md file.
Offers a simple reference for testing skill discovery and invocation.
Uses no bundled scripts, network calls, or external dependencies.
limitations: It only outputs one fixed greeting.
It does not accept parameters or customize the message.
It does not include tests, scripts, or integration logic.
It does not automate any broader workflow.

use_cases.title: Check Skill Installation
use_cases.description: Run a small greeting to confirm that an Enact skill can be discovered and invoked.

use_cases.title: Teach Skill Basics
use_cases.description: Show the smallest useful example of skill metadata, tags, and a fixed command.

use_cases.title: Start a New Example
use_cases.description: Use the simple greeting format as a starting point for a more useful internal skill.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Greeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Use enact-hello-simple to print the default greeting.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Example
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what enact-hello-simple does and why it is useful as a starter skill.

prompt_templates.title: Compare to a Real Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare enact-hello-simple with a production skill and list what would need to be added.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Derived Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use enact-hello-simple as a reference and outline a parameterized greeting skill with safe inputs.

output_examples.input: Use enact-hello-simple to print the greeting.

output_examples.output: This skill demonstrates the smallest Enact tool pattern: metadata, tags, and one fixed greeting command.
The skill only prints one fixed message and does not accept custom input.

best_practices: Use it as a smoke test before trying more complex skills.
Keep derived examples small until the command behavior is clear.
Document any new inputs or side effects when extending the example.
anti_patterns: Do not treat this example as a complete production workflow.
Do not add external commands without documenting their purpose and inputs.
Do not add network or file access to a greeting example without a clear need.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It prints the fixed message Hello from Enact.

faq.question: Is this skill intended for production work?
faq.answer: No. It is a minimal example for learning, testing, and scaffolding.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed skill contains no network behavior.

faq.question: Can I customize the greeting?
faq.answer: Not in this version. The greeting text is fixed by the skill command.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why is it useful?
faq.answer: It gives users a small, readable example before they build a more capable Enact skill.
